Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Stellaron Technologies Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Kim, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Janet Kim, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Stellaron Technologies’ Third Quarter 2024 earnings call. With me today are Alex Chen, CEO; Sarah Lee, CFO; David Park, COO; and Emily Carter, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our press release and earnings slides, which are available on our IR website. Please note that this call may contain forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Alex.

Alex Chen, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet, and welcome, everyone.

We had a strong quarter with performance driven by several key initiatives. First, I’d like to address our gross margin performance. Q3 2024 saw a notable improvement, driven primarily by successful cost reduction initiatives within our memory division and strategic pricing adjustments across key product lines. Our gross profit increased significantly, exceeding our initial guidance due to better-than-anticipated yields from advanced process migrations and favorable currency exchange rates. While macroeconomic headwinds persist, these internal improvements have allowed us to navigate the challenging environment and deliver solid results. In Q3 2024, our gross profit was W31.11 trillion, compared to W26.60 trillion in Q2 2024 and W28.50 trillion in Q3 2023. This translates to a gross margin of 43.2% in Q3 2024, compared to 42.5% in Q2 2024 and 41.8% in Q3 2023. The significant increase in gross profit QoQ is primarily attributable to our memory cost reductions via advanced process migrations, specifically the successful migration to our 176-layer NAND flash memory technology. This resulted in a 22% reduction in per-bit manufacturing costs compared to the previous generation, contributing approximately W2.8 trillion to the gross profit increase. We also saw strategic pricing adjustments in our display panel business, focusing on higher-margin OLED panels, which resulted in a 5% increase in the average selling price of display panels, contributing roughly W0.9 trillion to the gross profit improvement, despite a slight decrease in overall panel unit sales. Company-wide operational efficiency programs, including supply chain optimization and automation in manufacturing processes, yielded cost savings of approximately W0.5 trillion. Finally, a more favorable KRW/USD exchange rate positively impacted the gross profit by W0.31 trillion. Looking at the YoY improvement, which was more nuanced, key factors included the memory market beginning to show signs of recovery and our expansion into the automotive semiconductor market, where revenue increased by 35% YoY, adding W0.8 trillion to the gross profit. We exceeded our Q3 2024 gross margin guidance of 42.0% - 42.5% due to faster-than-expected yield improvements from the 176-layer NAND flash memory technology ramp-up, favorable currency exchange rates, stronger demand for high-end memory products, and effective inventory management. Specifically, sales of High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) for AI applications increased by 45% QoQ, exceeding our initial forecast of 30%.

We also made meaningful progress with our wafer sales this quarter. Q3 witnessed a moderately positive performance, driven primarily by ASP increases in both DRAM and NAND sectors. While wafer quantity growth was modest, the enhanced pricing environment allowed us to achieve a 7% increase in overall wafer revenue compared to Q2 and a 12% increase year-over-year to $3.85 billion. In DRAM, our bit growth landed in the low single digits, specifically at 3.5%, reflecting a cautious approach from our major customers. However, the key driver for DRAM revenue was a high-single-digit percentage increase in ASP, clocking in at 8.2%. This ASP increase is attributable to our continued successful migration to 1alpha DRAM production, representing roughly 45% of our total DRAM output, and a stronger-than-anticipated demand for high-density DRAM modules in the data center segment. In NAND, our bit growth reached a mid-single-digit percentage, specifically 5.5%, supported by increased demand from both the client SSD and enterprise SSD segments. The ASP for NAND increased by approximately 10%, reflecting a tightening supply-demand balance. Our ongoing development of 176-layer and now 232-layer NAND technology further enhanced our competitive position. The transition to 176-layer NAND represented approximately 70% of our total NAND output by the end of Q3.

On a broader level, our CapEx spending supported our positioning for future growth. Our Capital Expenditure for the third quarter totaled W10.21 trillion, a slight increase of 2.5% compared to Q3 2022. The cumulative CapEx for the year-to-date period now stands at W33.51 trillion, a 10.5% increase compared to the same period last year. In Q3, we invested W9.11 trillion in semiconductor-related projects, with a significant portion dedicated to expanding our DRAM and NAND flash memory production capacity, specifically at our Pyeongtaek Line 3 facility. We are also investing heavily in our 3nm and 2nm process nodes and enhancing our foundry capabilities to attract new customers. Recognizing the increasing importance of advanced packaging, we are investing in technologies such as 2.5D and 3D packaging. Our new packaging facility in Vietnam, which commenced operations in Q3, is already contributing to increased production capacity. Our display business received W0.71 trillion in CapEx, focusing on high-value OLED and QD-OLED technologies. We are continuing to invest in expanding our QD-OLED production capacity and improving the performance and efficiency of our mobile OLED panels. The construction of our new chip plant in Taylor, Texas, is still on track, with the first phase scheduled for completion in early 2025.

I’ll now hand it over to Sarah to walk you through the financials.

Sarah Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Alex, and hello, everyone.

This quarter’s financial results were underpinned by operational rigor and discipline. Let’s walk through the key metrics.

To start, our gross margin performance, as Alex outlined, helped drive improvements in our operating margin. In Q3 2024, our operating performance demonstrated significant strength, exceeding both our internal expectations and prior guidance. Operating profit increased by W3.31 trillion quarter-on-quarter to reach W15.8 trillion. This translated into an operating margin improvement of 1.6 percentage points. Year-on-year, the results were even more impressive, driven primarily by the robust performance of our component businesses. The primary driver was a significant uptick in our component businesses, specifically in memory chips and advanced display panels. We also implemented several operational efficiency initiatives, including supply chain optimization and increased automation. Our actual operating margin of 20.0% exceeded the upper end of our guidance of 19.0% to 19.5%, primarily due to an unforeseen surge in demand for our HBM memory solutions used in AI applications and better-than-expected yields in our advanced display panel manufacturing. We are raising our full-year operating margin guidance to 19.5%-20.0%, reflecting our confidence in our continued strong performance.

Additionally, our revenue performance showed strong growth. We achieved a total revenue of W74 trillion for the quarter, representing a robust 16.2% sequential (QoQ) increase compared to Q2 2024 and a significant 10.5% year-over-year (YoY) increase relative to Q3 2023. This QoQ growth is attributable to a substantial revenue jump in our Memory division and impressive resilience in our OLED Display division. The Memory division saw a 22% QoQ increase, primarily driven by increased demand for our next-generation DDR5 DRAM and high-density NAND flash memory. The OLED division achieved a 14% QoQ revenue increase, mainly due to increased demand for our flexible OLED panels. The 10.5% YoY revenue growth reflects the success of our long-term strategic initiatives and investments, including our continued leadership in memory technology and the diversification of our OLED business. We exceeded our revenue guidance of W72 trillion to W73 trillion, primarily driven by stronger-than-expected memory demand and the successful launch of our new line of flexible OLED panels.

Finally, looking at our sales by segment, the Mobile Business Unit demonstrated robust performance. Total MBU revenue was $2.3 billion, representing a 15% increase compared to Q3 2023. This growth was primarily fueled by smartphone sales, mobile accessories, and software and services. We saw strong uptake of the Apex X series in North America and strategic expansion in emerging markets like India and Southeast Asia. The MBU maintained a solid 12.5% operating profit margin, exceeding our internal target of 11%. This strong performance was achieved through a combination of a premium product mix, supply chain optimization, and cost control measures.

Now I’ll pass it to David to provide color on execution.

David Park, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

From a delivery and operations standpoint, this was one of our more efficient quarters in recent memory.

A big part of that was the capacity expansion plan we have underway, which allowed us to strategically allocate capital across our Memory, Foundry, and Display segments to capitalize on projected market demand and technological advancements. In the Memory division, we are investing in our ComTech facility in Xi'an, dedicating $450 million this quarter to expanding production capacity and migrating to more advanced process nodes, including 1alpha and 1beta. This expansion is projected to increase overall DRAM production capacity at the Xi'an facility by approximately 18% by the end of Q4, with a substantial portion dedicated to DDR5 production. In the Foundry division, we are investing $300 million this quarter to increase capacity for our 7nm and 5nm UV processes at the ComTech facility. In the Display division, we are investing $200 million in upgrading our existing OLED display production lines to incorporate QD technology and $100 million in expanding our capacity for manufacturing mobile display modules.

We also saw execution gains related to our wafer sales performance, including our ability to meet the increasing demand for high-density DRAM modules and our strategic partnerships with key customers. Asia-Pacific continued to be our largest DRAM market, accounting for approximately 60% of sales, but we saw the strongest growth in North America, driven by robust demand from hyperscale data centers.

Lastly, we began pilots tied to new QD Display technologies, where early signs are promising. We are investing in upgrading our existing OLED display production lines to incorporate QD technology. The goal is to convert 25% of the existing OLED production capacity to QD-OLED by the end of the year.

Now I’ll turn it over to Emily to discuss technology.

Emily Carter, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, David.

On the technology side, our teams delivered important milestones across multiple streams.

First, we completed major feature work aligned with our wafer sales strategy, especially our ongoing development of 176-layer and now 232-layer NAND technology which further enhanced our competitive position. The transition to 176-layer NAND represented approximately 70% of our total NAND output by the end of Q3. We also introduced a new line of PCIe Gen5 SSDs based on 232-layer NAND, which received positive initial feedback from customers.

We also rolled out enhancements supporting our sales by segment, specifically the Mobile Business Unit. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to develop cutting-edge mobile technologies, including advanced camera systems, AI-powered features, and enhanced 5G connectivity. We are also exploring opportunities in augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) applications for mobile devices.

One final point — we’ve made structural improvements to better enable our CapEx strategy, allowing us to accelerate investments in developing alternative component sourcing strategies and exploring new supply chain partnerships. This includes expanding our relationships with smaller, more agile suppliers and investing in internal chip design capabilities to reduce our reliance on external vendors in the long run.

Let’s now open the floor for Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. You mentioned gains in the operating margin. What gives you confidence that these are sustainable?

Alex Chen:
We are confident in our ability to sustain our operating margin momentum due to our strategic focus on high-value component businesses, continued operational excellence, and investments in R&D. We are also closely monitoring potential risks, such as geopolitical uncertainties and increased competition, and are prepared to take proactive measures to mitigate their impact.

Analyst 2:
On the gross margin, is this level sustainable given the potential for memory price fluctuations?

Sarah Lee:
While memory prices are subject to fluctuations, we believe our gross margin is sustainable due to our technology leadership, cost reduction initiatives, and expansion into higher-margin product segments. We are also actively managing our inventory levels and hedging against potential price declines.

Analyst 3:
Can you elaborate on early traction with the new QD Display technology?

David Park:
We are seeing positive initial feedback from customers on our new QD-OLED displays, particularly in the premium TV and monitor markets. The improved color gamut and brightness of these displays are resonating well with consumers, and we are securing design wins with leading TV manufacturers. We expect continued strong demand for our QD-OLED displays in the coming quarters.

Analyst 4:
How are you thinking about long-term opportunity in alternative component sourcing?

Emily Carter:
We view alternative component sourcing as a critical strategic initiative to enhance our supply chain resilience and reduce our reliance on single suppliers. We are actively exploring partnerships with new suppliers and investing in internal chip design capabilities to diversify our sourcing options and mitigate potential disruptions. This will not only improve our cost competitiveness but also enhance our ability to respond quickly to changing market conditions.

Closing

Alex Chen:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us. We’re energized by the results this quarter and remain focused on disciplined execution and strategic expansion. Looking forward to sharing continued progress next time.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
